name: Zoldonrasib
summary: Zoldonrasib (RMC-9805) is Revolution Medicines' oral, covalent RAS(ON) G12D-selective tri-complex inhibitor, taken daily to progression. The modelled Phase 3 is RASolve 308 (NCT07777822, n=430, primary completion 2029-10): zoldonrasib or placebo added to pembrolizumab, pemetrexed and platinum in first-line metastatic non-squamous RAS G12D NSCLC, a design twin of SUNRAY-01 Part B in the olomorasib (LY3537982) seed. The pancreatic Phase 3s (RASolute 305, NCT07621718, primary completion 2028-12-30; RASolute 309, NCT07805954, 2029-03) read out first and address a larger population, but are not modelled: the book carries no pancreatic pool, and the Royalty Pharma royalty reaches zoldonrasib wherever its label sits inside a daraxonrasib one, which first-line PDAC would once RASolute 303 succeeds. Price: Lumakras at $98,285 per 2024 CMS Part D beneficiary, the anchor all three G12C seeds use; RVMD's own RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) WAC of $39,800 per 30 days is the case against. Uptake: the G12C seeds' 0.3387, 0.65 times the measured Lumakras plus Krazati class capture, a judgement. Ex-US: Lumakras's own filed split, 0.72.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07777822 (book trials table: randomised, double-blind, PFS primary endpoint); oral once-daily dosing at 1200 mg in the Phase 1 (AACR news release, April 2026 (aacr.org/about-the-aacr/newsroom/news-releases/investigational-krason-inhibitor-zoldonrasib-showed-effective-and-durable-responses-in-patients-with-advanced-g12d-mutated-lung-cancer/)); RVMD 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-335104): 'oral RAS(ON) G12D-selective tri-complex inhibitor'
therapy_mode.note: Oral daily tablet added to pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum in advanced disease, taken until progression, so chronic by the house definition
therapy_mode.check: RVMD 10-Q Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-335104, book filing_sections): 'Zoldonrasib is designed as an oral RAS(ON) G12D-selective tri-complex inhibitor'. AACR 2026 coverage (aacr.org news release; OncLive; Oncology Central, found by search): RP2D 1200 mg once daily, taken continuously. RASolve 308 (NCT07777822, book trials table: randomised, double-blind, PFS primary; registry summary via search) adds zoldonrasib or placebo to pembrolizumab + pemetrexed + platinum in first-line metastatic disease, so to progression: chronic by the house definition.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Lumakras: CMS Part D 2024, $153,620,120.69 over 1,563 beneficiaries = $98,285
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement: house convention and the anchor of the LY3537982, calderasib and divarasib seeds, as the brief for this asset asked. Lumakras (sotorasib) is the first approved KRAS allele-selective inhibitor in NSCLC and oral like zoldonrasib; no G12D-directed drug is marketed. Case against, and it is strong: RVMD priced its first RAS(ON) inhibitor, RASONQUE (daraxonrasib, approved 2026-08-26 in previously treated metastatic PDAC), at a WAC of $39,800 per 30-day supply (RVMD 8-K 0001193125-26-366931), about $484,000 a year at WAC. That is a list price before rebates on a full-year basis and in another disease, so it is not like-for-like with a CMS per-beneficiary figure, which already carries part-year use; but if payers read zoldonrasib's price off RASONQUE rather than Lumakras, this anchor is several times too low. Krazati's 2024 figure is lower at $66,903 (second launch year). A first-line add-on to pembrolizumab-chemotherapy could be priced either way.
list_price_per_patient.check: Arithmetic: lookup.py demand Lumakras, Part D 2024, $153,620,120.69 / 1,563 beneficiaries = $98,285.43, so 0.098285 mm USD per patient-year is right in unit and value; Krazati 2024 $66,903 also matches. Same anchor, value and unit as the LY3537982 and calderasib seeds (divarasib carries it CHF-converted). ANCHOR SETTLED: the brief's convention is 'the closest marketed comparator in the same disease and setting', and its 'published annual list price beats the convention' has been applied in this book only to a comparator in the same disease (Qinlock for velzatinib, Voyxact for zigakibart). RASONQUE is a published WAC ($39,800 per 30-day supply, RVMD 8-K 0001193125-26-366931, read in the book: '$39,800 for a 30-day supply, based on the recommended daily dose'; $484,233 a year at 365/30) but it is a different molecule approved only in previously treated metastatic PDAC, so it is not in the same disease or setting, and a WAC would also need a sourced discount, which does not exist for a drug launched on 2026-08-26. The rules therefore support Lumakras, not RASONQUE, for a second RAS(ON) inhibitor from the same company. PART-YEAR QUESTION: the engine (backend/forecast.py treated_stock) runs stock(t) = stock(t-1) x (1 - d) + new(t) and bills the whole stock a full year, so every starter is billed a full first year and every stopper is dropped for the whole year. At d = 0.5273 that stock is 1.90 x annual starts at steady state, against 1.33 x in patient-years (constant hazard, mean 1.33 years) and 2.33 x in distinct patients treated in a year, the CMS beneficiary basis. So the engine's stock is a headcount close to CMS beneficiaries, and a per-beneficiary price is the matching unit; the divarasib seed also solved the capture from beneficiary counts. A full-year WAC on this stock would overstate revenue by about 1.42x. The engine's persistence therefore already absorbs most of the part-year effect; at steady state the per-beneficiary price times the engine stock is about 0.81 of true gross. Two residuals both run low, and neither is a sourced price, so the value stands: (1) Lumakras's figure embeds Lumakras's own short second-line use, 8,675 claims / 1,563 beneficiaries = 5.55 fills (about $17,708 gross a fill) against about 6.9 months per beneficiary implied by this seed's 0.5273; (2) gross_to_net.py records the halving at 65% of the negotiated price for Imbruvica, the oral oncology drug in its calibration, against a 96% median. Case for higher also stands: zoldonrasib's pancreatic Phase 3 (RASolute 305) reads out ten months before RASolve 308, so its launch price may be struck in PDAC beside RASONQUE, at 2.25x Lumakras's gross per fill. Judgement labelled, case against stated in the note.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS Part D per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py: halving lands at a median 96% of CMS's negotiated net prices across the cycle-one IRA drugs); Lumakras sits in Part D (lookup.py demand Lumakras)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 is the share OFF list, so net is $49,143 a patient-year. Zoldonrasib is oral and would sit in Part D. Same value as the three G12C seeds. If the RASONQUE WAC were used as the anchor instead, 0.5 would not apply and a sourced WAC discount would be needed
gross_to_net_pct.check: Direction: 0.5 is the share OFF list, so net = 0.098285 x 0.5 = $49,143 a patient-year. The anchor is a Part D figure (lookup.py demand Lumakras returns part 'D' only), so the Part D convention of 0.5 applies, not 0.056604. backend/gross_to_net.py states the median 96% of CMS negotiated prices across the nine cycle-one drugs. Matches the LY3537982, calderasib and divarasib seeds. Correct that a RASONQUE WAC anchor would need its own sourced discount; none is filed.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: median PFS 11.1 months (95% CI 5.3 to not estimable) in 27 patients with previously treated KRAS G12D NSCLC at the 1200 mg daily Phase 2 dose, confirmed ORR 52% (AACR news release, April 2026 (aacr.org/about-the-aacr/newsroom/news-releases/investigational-krason-inhibitor-zoldonrasib-showed-effective-and-durable-responses-in-patients-with-advanced-g12d-mutated-lung-cancer/); also Cancer Discovery news, doi:10.1158/2159-8290.CD-NW2026-0040)
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard fitted to the median, as the divarasib seed does with its own monotherapy PFS and the LY3537982 seed with its own: 1 - 0.5^(12/11.1) = 0.527. The brief's 1 - exp(-12/11.1) gives 0.661 but treats the median as a mean. Case against: n=27 with a wide interval, second-line monotherapy rather than the RASolve 308 regimen; adding zoldonrasib to the first-line KEYNOTE-189 backbone (PFS HR 0.50 for pembrolizumab over chemotherapy alone, Garassino et al., JCO 2023, doi:10.1200/JCO.22.01989) aims to lengthen PFS, which would lower this rate. The first-line combination data (RVMD 8-K 0001193125-26-335039) have 3.4 months of follow-up and no PFS. The book's advanced-tumour convention, 0.55 (calderasib seed), sits close.
discontinuation_pct.check: Search (aacr.org news release, AACR 2026; OncLive; Oncology Central): 27 evaluable previously treated KRAS G12D NSCLC patients at 1200 mg daily, confirmed ORR 52% (95% CI 32-71%), DCR 93%, median PFS 11.1 months, 12-month OS 73%. Recomputed 1 - 0.5^(12/11.1) = 0.52733 (the brief's 1 - exp(-12/11.1) = 0.6608, disclosed). Median-based hazard is the method of the divarasib (0.47 from 13.1 mo) and LY3537982 (0.506 from 11.8 mo) seeds. Not seen: the PFS interval '5.3 to not estimable', and the Cancer Discovery news DOI 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-NW2026-0040 (not indexed in PubMed; a PubMed search for zoldonrasib in 2026 returns 10 records, none of it). The value rests on the AACR release, which holds. The first-line combination data (8-K 0001193125-26-335039, read in the book): 38 patients, 28 evaluable, median follow-up 3.4 months, ORR 82%, no PFS, as the note says.

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07777822 primary completion 2029-10, estimated (context file; book trials table, last update 2026-08-20)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on timing. Book convention (calderasib and LY3537982 seeds): first full year two calendar years after the Phase 3 primary completion, so readout late 2029, filing 2030, launch late 2030, 2031 the first full year. The asset's earliest Phase 3 primary completion is RASolute 305 in pancreatic cancer (2028-12-30), which would give 2030 if that indication were modelled; NSCLC revenue cannot start before its own readout. Case for earlier: FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation in December 2025 (RVMD FY2025 10-K 0001193125-26-071563; press coverage dates it January 2026) for previously treated KRAS G12D NSCLC, with a Phase 2 monotherapy expansion still following patients (10-Q Q2 2026). An accelerated second-line approval would come earlier, but in a different line and pool, and RVMD has stated no such filing. LOE: no molecule patent date is filed. Revolution's FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-071563, patents section) gives only a 2031 to 2045 range across its tri-complex RAS portfolio, with no date for zoldonrasib, so the engine's default applies: 12 years from this launch year, 2043. No date is written here because none is filed
forecast_start_year.check: defect review 2026-09-25: value unchanged; the note now states that no molecule patent date is filed and the engine's 12-year default applies; was 2031 (confirmed)

exus_multiple.source: Amgen FY2025 10-K (0000318154-26-000010) MD&A product sales table: LUMAKRAS U.S. $211mm, LUMYKRAS ROW $152mm (FY2024 $214mm and $136mm); the Q4 2025 release (8-K 0000318154-26-000003) ties: U.S. 211, ROW 152, total 363. 152 / 211 = 0.7204
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Lumakras is the direct analogue: an oral KRAS allele-selective NSCLC drug with a filed geographic split. RVMD has no marketed product with a full year of sales. Case against: RVMD has no ex-US commercial organisation yet (it only began an EMA phased review of daraxonrasib, Q2 2026 release), so ex-US launch timing or a partner's cut is unknown; Lumakras's ratio is lifted by a US label held to second line after the CodeBreaK 200 complete response letter; FY2024 read 0.636. Krazati reads 0.068 (13/192, BMS FY2025 10-K 0000014272-26-000004, book asset_revenue_regions), the low case, because its ex-US rights and launches lag. The LY3537982 seed's Verzenio 0.6521 and the calderasib seed's Keytruda 0.680 sit close to this value.
exus_multiple.check: Amgen FY2025 10-K (0000318154-26-000010) product sales table, read in the book: 'LUMAKRAS - U.S. 211 (1)% 214 9% 197; LUMYKRAS - ROW 152 12% 136 64% 83'. Q4 2025 release (8-K 0000318154-26-000003): full year 211 + 152 = 363 against 350. 152 / 211 = 0.72038; FY2024 136 / 214 = 0.6355. Krazati: book asset_revenue_regions FY2025 US $192mm, INTL $13mm = 0.0677 (BMS 10-K 0000014272-26-000004). Comparator choice is a labelled judgement with its low case stated.

economics_share.source: RVMD 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-335104), Note 8, and FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-071563), Note 10: Royalty Pharma's revenue participation right covers RMC-9805 (zoldonrasib) Products only 'if an RMC-9805 Product is approved for the same indication or subset of the same indication for which an RMC-6236 Product is approved'. RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) approval, 2026-08-26, 'for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy' (RVMD 8-K 0001193125-26-366931)
economics_share.note: Wholly owned: zoldonrasib comes from RVMD's own RAS(ON) discovery pipeline, and the filings name no licensor or co-development partner; the Summit (ivonescimab) and Tango collaborations are clinical combination studies with no stated economics on zoldonrasib. Daraxonrasib's only approval is in pancreatic cancer and its NSCLC Phase 3 (RASolve 301) is in previously treated disease, so a first-line G12D NSCLC label does not sit inside a daraxonrasib indication today and the royalty does not attach. Case against: if daraxonrasib later wins a first-line NSCLC label (RVMD is testing it with PD-(L)1/VEGF bispecifics), the royalty attaches at 4.55% of annual net sales up to $2.0bn, 2.50% from $2.0bn to $4.0bn and 1.00% from $4.0bn to $8.0bn after the two tranches drawn, rising to 7.80%, 4.55% and 2.40% if tranches 3 to 5 are drawn, with an upward adjustment in 2030 to 2041 on the first tier if sales fall short. RVMD has no cost rows in the book, so the netting (margin - royalty) / margin cannot be computed yet. Second reader's case against: the 10-Q defines the royalty base as worldwide net product sales of RMC-9805 Products once an RMC-9805 Product is approved in an indication inside an RMC-6236 one, and does not say the base is only that indication. Royalty Pharma's release ('zoldonrasib if approved in an overlapping daraxonrasib indication') supports the per-indication reading used here. If the agreement is product-wide, a first-line G12D PDAC approval from RASolute 305 (primary completion 2028-12-30), inside a first-line daraxonrasib PDAC label from RASolute 303 (2028-06), would bring the NSCLC sales under the royalty before 2031. The tiers are struck on combined daraxonrasib and zoldonrasib sales, so the marginal rate would most likely be 2.50%, 1.00% or nil. Tranche 3's trigger was met by the 2026-08-26 approval; no draw is filed yet
economics_share.check: VALUE 1.0 CONFIRMED; NOTE CORRECTED to add a case against the researcher left out. Royalty confirmed from the filing: RVMD 10-Q Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-335104), Note 8, read in the book: Royalty Pharma bought 'tiered royalty payments with respect to worldwide net product sales of (i) RMC-6236 Products and (ii) RMC-9805 Products, if an RMC-9805 Product is approved for the same indication or subset of the same indication for which an RMC-6236 Product is approved'; after the upfront $250mm and the May 2026 Tranche 2 $250mm, '4.55% of annual net sales up to $2.0 billion, 2.50% ... $2.0 billion and $4.0 billion, 1.00% ... $4.0 billion and $8.0 billion, and no Royalty Payments on sales in excess of $8.0 billion'; 7.80%, 4.55% and 2.40% if Tranches 3 to 5 are all bought; an upward adjustment on the $0 to $2bn tier in 2030 to 2041 that 'remains in the single digits'; obligations end on the fifteenth anniversary of the first US commercial sale of an RMC-6236 Product. Tranche 3's trigger (FDA approval in second-line metastatic PDAC before 2028-07-01) was met on 2026-08-26 (8-K 0001193125-26-366931); no filing seen that RVMD has drawn it. APPLICATION TO THE MODELLED INDICATION: RMC-6236's only approval is metastatic PDAC after prior therapy or unfit for multiagent therapy; its NSCLC Phase 3, RASolve 301 (NCT06881784), is 'locally advanced or metastatic RAS mutant NSCLC who have been treated with immunotherapy and platinum-containing chemotherapy' (10-Q), and RVMD says it is 'prioritizing a mutant-selective approach for development in 1L NSCLC', with daraxonrasib in 1L NSCLC only with PD-1/VEGF bispecifics and no Phase 3 (10-Q; book trials table lists none). A first-line G12D label is not a subset of a previously treated one, so no royalty applies to the modelled indication today, and the brief's netting and refusal rules are not engaged. Royalty Pharma's release as surfaced by search ('zoldonrasib if approved in an overlapping daraxonrasib indication'), and trade press saying zoldonrasib in exclusive indications would not incur royalty, support reading the royalty as limited to overlapping indications. No licensor: the 10-K names Warp Drive Bio as a 2018 acquisition (wholly owned), the Sanofi SHP2 agreement ended June 2023, and the Summit, Tango, BMS and Synnovation deals are clinical collaborations. lookup.py seed on daraxonrasib, RMC-6236 and elironrasib returns nothing, so RVMD has no cost rows. Case against added to the note: the filed wording makes the royalty base 'worldwide net product sales of ... RMC-9805 Products' once any one zoldonrasib approval overlaps. By the 2031 start, a first-line G12D PDAC approval from RASolute 305 (primary completion 2028-12-30) would sit inside a first-line PDAC daraxonrasib label if RASolute 303 (NCT07491445, 2028-06) succeeds. On a product-wide reading the NSCLC sales would then carry the royalty. The filed tiers are struck on combined annual net sales, so zoldonrasib would most likely fall in the 2.50%, 1.00% or nil tiers once RASONQUE passes $2bn.

prevalence.note: Carried by the book, prevalence equal to incidence under its oncology convention; the same pool the three G12C seeds use

incidence.check: epidemiology.csv incidence 192,650, equal to prevalence under the oncology convention. Null is right.

eligible_pct.source: Three filters. (1) KRAS G12D in 684 of 17,095 NSCLC specimens, 4.00% (Judd et al., 'Characterization of KRAS Mutation Subtypes in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer', Mol Cancer Ther 2021;20(12):2577-2584, doi:10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-21-0201, PMID 34518295, Table 1; Caris, the paper the calderasib seed already cites for PD-L1). (2) 51% distant stage at diagnosis (SEER 21, the calderasib and LY3537982 seeds). (3) 79% of US stage IV NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations start first-line therapy (2,904 of 3,661; Abernethy et al., PLoS One 2017, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0178420, the LY3537982 and ABBV-1480 seeds' share). 0.04001 x 0.51 x 0.79 = 0.016121, about 3,106 patients a year on 192,650. Population: NCT07777822 eligibility (ClinicalTrials.gov): previously untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with a documented RAS G12D mutation, known PD-L1 status, ECOG 0-1, no prior RAS-directed therapy
eligible_pct.note: No PD-L1 filter: the first-line Phase 1 cohort enrolled at every PD-L1 level (TPS <1% in 39%, 1-49% in 39%, 50% or more in 16%; RVMD Q2 2026 release, 8-K 0001193125-26-335039) and the pembrolizumab-pemetrexed-platinum backbone is labelled regardless of PD-L1, as in the LY3537982 seed. RASolve 308's eligibility (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07777822) requires previously untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with a documented RAS G12D mutation and a known PD-L1 status, with no PD-L1 threshold, so no PD-L1 filter applies. Case for higher: Judd's G12C share (1,882 of 17,095, 11.0%) sits below the 13.8% GENIE figure the G12C seeds use, so this Caris cohort may understate allele shares against GENIE; and the trial's 'RAS G12D' includes NRAS and HRAS G12D, which Judd does not count. Case for lower: the 4.0% includes squamous tumours the trial excludes (KRAS is mutated in 4.4% of squamous against 37.2% of adenocarcinoma, so the effect is small), and the 51% is all lung cancer, where SCLC skews distant. Stage IV recurrences after early-stage disease are left out, which understates the pool.
eligible_pct.check: VALUE CONFIRMED; NOTE AND SOURCE CORRECTED because the researcher had not read the trial's eligibility. (1) PubMed full text of Judd et al., Mol Cancer Ther 2021 (PMID 34518295, PMC9662933, doi:10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-21-0201), Table 1: G12D 684 (15% of 4,706 KRAS-mutant) of 17,095 NSCLC; G12C 1,882. 684 / 17,095 = 0.040012. KRAS mutated in 37.2% of adenocarcinoma and 4.4% of squamous; subtype distribution similar in both histologies. (2) 51% distant stage and (3) 79% (2,904 of 3,661) starting first-line therapy are the shares the LY3537982, calderasib and ABBV-1480 seeds carry (lookup.py pool). Recomputed 0.040012 x 0.51 x 0.79 = 0.016121, x 192,650 = 3,106 a year. Same funnel as the LY3537982 seed (0.138 x 0.51 x 0.79 = 0.0556) with G12D swapped for G12C, so the book's first-line KRAS add-ons stay comparable. Eligibility (NCT07777822, ClinicalTrials.gov, summarised by search): previously untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with documented RAS G12D, ECOG 0-1, 'known PD-L1 status', prior RAS-directed therapy excluded. So there is no PD-L1 cut, which confirms leaving out a PD-L1 filter, and the line is first line. The Phase 1 cohort's PD-L1 spread (<1% 39%, 1-49% 39%, >=50% 16%) is confirmed in the 8-K exhibit (0001193125-26-335039). Uncorrected residuals roughly offset: the squamous tumours in the 4.0% (the trial excludes them) against NRAS/HRAS G12D and stage IV recurrences, which the funnel omits.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the eligible untreated pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: reused from the LY3537982 and divarasib seeds: lookup.py demand Lumakras and Krazati give CMS Part D beneficiaries of 1,527 + 443 = 1,970 in 2023 and 1,563 + 1,042 = 2,605 in 2024; the divarasib seed solves this to new starts equal to 52.1% of the Medicare-eligible G12C second line (midpoint of 46.2% and 58.0% at 55% and 77.4% discontinuation)
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: 0.65 x 52.1% = 0.3387, the multiple the first-line G12C seeds use, kept so the book's first-line KRAS allele-selective add-ons carry one capture, as the brief for this asset asked. Case for higher: the 0.65 reflects a first line split among four G12C entrants; RASolve 308 is the only first-line G12D NSCLC Phase 3 in the book's trials table, no RAS-targeted therapy is approved for G12D NSCLC (ILCN/WCLC and ASCO Post coverage, 2026; daraxonrasib's approval is in pancreatic cancer), and RVMD says it is prioritising a mutant-selective approach in first-line NSCLC (10-Q Q2 2026). At 1.0x the value is 0.521. The nearest rivals are later or elsewhere: GenFleet's GFH375 (Verastem's VS-7375) in a Phase 3 against docetaxel in previously treated disease, and Astellas's setidegrasib entering Phase 3 in lung cancer. Case for lower: the 52.1% was measured in second line, where a G12C inhibitor was the only targeted option, and is applied to a first line where pembrolizumab-chemotherapy alone stays standard; RVMD's own daraxonrasib also covers G12D; the calderasib seed's 0.20 is the lower case.
penetration_peak_pct.check: Inputs from the helper: Lumakras Part D beneficiaries 1,527 (2023) and 1,563 (2024); Krazati 443 and 1,042; sums 1,970 and 2,605. lookup.py seed: the divarasib and LY3537982 seeds both carry 0.3387 = 0.65 x 52.1% (midpoint of 46.2% and 58.0%). Recomputed 0.65 x 0.521 = 0.33865. It is a labelled judgement on confirmed inputs; at peak it gives about 1,052 US starts a year on 3,106 eligible. The trial population matches the pool (first-line, RAS G12D, non-squamous, any PD-L1). CANNIBALISATION SETTLED: RVMD has no marketed or Phase 3 product in first-line NSCLC except this trial. RASONQUE's label is PDAC only (8-K 0001193125-26-366931). Daraxonrasib's NSCLC Phase 3 RASolve 301 and its Breakthrough designation cover previously treated non-G12C KRAS NSCLC (10-Q). RVMD prioritises mutant-selective drugs in first line, with RASolve 307 (elironrasib) in G12C, a different allele. So zoldonrasib in RASolve 308 takes no patients from an RVMD marketed product, and the hold rule (as for nucresiran, ibuzatrelvir, PG4) does not apply. It would apply in PDAC, which is not modelled: RASolute 305 zoldonrasib 1L G12D PDAC would compete with daraxonrasib's RASolute 303 1L PDAC and with RASONQUE's current label, which already reaches first-line patients unfit for multiagent therapy. The only NSCLC overlap is later-line sequencing into a possible daraxonrasib second-line label, a pipeline-on-pipeline effect with no daraxonrasib seed in the book to double count.
